name: Minisoft hourly builder
prompt:
Continue the user's Minisoft series in /Users/lucaschu/code/minisoft. On this hourly wake, claim or resume exactly one of the 100 supplied ideas and build a useful, working release in its numbered apps/ subfolder. Start with MiniHackathon (source #33), then #1–32, then #34–100 as recorded in catalog/ideas.json. This is one coherent suite with a shared foundation; ordinary workflows should operate without live model calls. Preserve the user's source briefs and approval boundaries.

First read /Users/lucaschu/code/minisoft/AGENTS.md and docs/runbook.md, then run python3 scripts/factory.py status, next, and validate from that root. The ledger, actual product files, and receipts are authoritative. Read only the selected product and relevant dependencies. Claim through the factory CLI using an actual coordinator identifier; do not manually edit completion state. Respect the exclusive lease. Skip overlapping active work quietly. Recover an expired lease only after verifying its coordinator, children, and relevant processes stopped, using the explicit recovery flags and an evidence-based note. Renew during long work, and stop/join children before releasing the lease.

Write or refresh the product's SPEC.md using docs/product-contract.md. Implement the primary end-to-end workflow from the original idea, with appropriate persistence, validation, meaningful errors, export/recovery, and truthful limitations. For later high-consequence products, preserve the source's sandbox, human approval, and independent-review boundaries. Do not substitute an empty dashboard or generic CRUD for specialized behavior. Grow shared packages from actual consumers, keep domain operations separate from provider adapters, and update the linked design documents and decisions when the implementation proves a better contract.

Use the optimal number of collaboration subagents for useful parallel work (tokenmaxx). With four available slots, normally use the coordinator plus up to three children for domain/data logic, UI/workflows, and independent verification. Assign disjoint file ownership and concrete acceptance/evidence requirements. Use fewer for a small product or overlapping work, reuse idle agents, and inherit this chat's model/effort. Optimize verified useful output, not token consumption. The coordinator integrates, owns shared contracts/state, publishes, and accepts. Do not fan out multiple products in the same wake.

Run appropriate checks and exercise the actual UI/runtime from representative input to usable output. Verify relevant constraints/calculations, error paths, persistence after reload/restart, access boundaries, and exports. Obtain an independent review, fix material findings, and preserve evidence. Use the relevant installed skills and tools. Build success alone does not prove runtime behavior; local storage does not provide shared-team access controls.

Whenever a website is created or edited, publish it in this same task through its existing hosting provider/site, preserving audience/domain, without asking for deployment permission again. Read and reuse actual hosting metadata. If no provider exists, use the Sites building and hosting skills where appropriate and prefer a single private Minisoft hub with stable product routes. Record the actual IDs; never invent or recreate them. Publish the exact verified source state and verify terminal succeeded status plus expected served revision. If publishing is blocked, preserve verified local work and record what remains unpublished; do not mark it complete. Real messages to people or other consequential actions still require the source's explicit authorization/approval.

Keep product README.md/SPEC.md accurate. Save a receipt using the exact factory schema with source digest, changed files, successful check commands and evidence, core runtime evidence, persistence/export checks or justified non-applicability, independent review, limitations, and website success/URL/evidence when applicable. Accept through complete --run <actual-run-id> --receipt <actual-path> only after applicable gates pass. The script checks structure; you must verify the truth. Stop after this product. If unfinished, checkpoint exact next steps and resume on a later wake; complex ideas may span hours. Mark genuine external prerequisites blocked so other queued ideas can proceed, and unblock when prerequisites change. Aim to checkpoint before the next hourly wake, leaving time for verification/publication. Do not create catch-up bursts for missed runs.

Count 100 distinct accepted products, not 100 invocations. If no product is eligible but fewer than 100 are accepted, cheaply inspect recorded blocked prerequisites, unblock only when something changed, and otherwise stay quiet; an empty eligible queue is not completion. When all 100 are accepted, disable this existing heartbeat through Codex's automation tool using state/automation.json, preserving its other fields, verify the returned inactive state, save it, and report completion once. If disabling fails, subsequent wakes must perform no product work and retry disabling. Never archive this chat automatically.

Stay quiet while state is unchanged, work overlaps, or a known blocker remains non-actionable. Notify the user concisely only on a verified release, meaningful change, new failure/blocker requiring action, or series completion. Include the product path, live URL when verified, useful workflow delivered, checks, limitations, and accepted count. Do not claim any planned folder is already built.
instructions: Manage this existing heartbeat with Codex automation_update. Use mode update, this automation_id as id, and target_thread_id as targetThreadId, preserving kind, name, prompt, rrule, destination and notification settings. Inspect current scheduler fields before updating. Do not edit scheduler storage.
